writeup: TIC 246650797 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 14.546769 days. The system shows a primary eclipse causing a 5.75 percent dimming of light, along with a secondary eclipse detected at 6.7 sigma significance. Automated analysis of TESS photometry data produced a strong detection signal with a signal-to-noise ratio of 168.0, and pixel-level imaging confirmed the eclipse signature with a peak signal-to-noise of 24.4. However, the eclipses show significantly alternating depths, suggesting the initially calculated period was actually half the true orbital period. This candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new system worthy of further study.
